newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on stocks' shortage.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on stocks' shortage.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Monday rose on a shortage of ready stock and lower arrivals at producing centres, dealers said.
Gujarat region produce fell following unseasonal rains in the region, one broker said.
Last week, arrivals in the Punjab region dropped considerably but Gujarat arrivals were steady.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 5/10 rupees at 1,000/1,030 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 rose by 10 rupees at 2,040/2,060 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) climbed up by 100 rupees at 14,600/15,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton rose by 100 rupees at 13,400 rupees per candy.

"Overall sentiments remained firm during the day amid limited supplies but looking at the sluggish mill buying and progress of the monsoon, cotton prices may attract profit-taking at the higher level," he said.
